# k0rdent_vpcs (Data Source)

Every VPC in a project.

A VPC comes with a cluster or an instance group and is never created directly. To name a cluster's VPC in a resource, use the cluster's `vpc` attribute rather than this data source: a data source that depends on the cluster is read at apply whenever the cluster has a pending change, which makes the VPC id unknown and replaces everything that names it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every VPC in the project, for inspection. To name a cluster's VPC in a
# resource, use the cluster's `vpc` attribute instead.
data "k0rdent_vpcs" "all" {}

output "vpcs_by_owner" {
  value = { for v in data.k0rdent_vpcs.all.vpcs : v.id => v.owner_kind }
}

# VPCs still being updated.
data "k0rdent_vpcs" "settling" {
  state = "updating"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the VPCs whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `state` (String) Return only the VPCs whose `state` is this value. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["creating" "active" "updating" "deleting" "failed"].

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) Just the ids, at the same positions as `vpcs`. Sorted by `id`.
- `vpcs` (Attributes List) The VPCs. Sorted by `id`. That order is stable when the platform reorders its response but not when a VPC is added, since a new `id` sorting first shifts every index: prefer `for_each` over `ids` to `vpcs[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vpcs))

<a id="nestedatt--vpcs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vpcs`

Read-Only:

- `backend` (String) Fabric backend serving the VPC. Only a `nico` VPC can carry security groups; on any other backend `security_groups` is always empty and attaching one is refused.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `id` (String) The VPC's name.
- `owner_id` (String) UID of the owning cluster or instance group.
- `owner_kind` (String) What materialized this VPC: a cluster or an instance group. Deleting that owner deletes the VPC.
- `security_groups` (List of String) Ids of the attached security groups, in the order they were last set. Never empty on a `nico` VPC: clearing the binding reinstates the platform's DEFAULT group rather than leaving none.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this VPC.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state. `updating` means a security-group change has been accepted and `security_groups` is what the API will converge on, not necessarily what the fabric enforces yet.
- `ufo_cr_name` (String) The VPC's fabric name. This is the value a cluster-provisioned `k0rdent_network` reports as `vpc`.
